ui/_win_raise.py — reliably raise a Tk window to the foreground on Windows.

The naive ``lift()`` + ``focus_force()`` used before V2.0.19.7 is unreliable on
Windows: clicking the taskbar button hands the foreground token to
``explorer.exe``; by the time Tk's ``<Map>`` handler runs in-process the token
has expired, so ``SetForegroundWindow`` (called internally by ``focus_force``)
is silently rejected by the foreground lock. The window restores but stays
behind other apps — the classic "taskbar shows running but nothing pops up"
bug.

Fix strategy (Windows only):
  1. deiconify if the window is minimized;
  2. toggle ``-topmost`` True -> update -> False, which forces the window past
     the foreground lock even without a valid foreground token;
  3. ``ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_RESTORE)`` to normalize/restore the window;
  4. ``SetForegroundWindow(hwnd)`` to pull it forward.

Non-Windows platforms fall back to ``lift()`` + ``focus_force()``.

This module imports only the standard library so neither ``ui.main_window`` nor
``ui.recipe_dialog`` creates a circular import when they import it.
Return the user32 ctypes lib on Windows, else None.

Bring *win* (a ``tkinter`` Toplevel / Tk) to the front reliably.

    Every step is guarded so a failure degrades gracefully to the old
    ``lift``/``focus_force`` behaviour rather than raising an exception inside
    a Tk event handler.
